title: 00 — What's New: Index
html:
00 — What's New: Index

The one idea: new tools and releases are only worth your time once you know what problem they solve, what they replace, and what it takes to try them. Each note here answers those three questions for one release, in the same shape every time.

1. What this set covers

One note per notable release or announcement in software engineering and AI: new language and framework versions, model and tooling releases, cloud services, databases and developer tools. Notes are added by a daily scheduled job and reviewed before they are published.

Every note follows the same structure:

  1. What it is: the release in plain words, who made it, and when.
  2. Why it matters: the problem it solves and what it changes compared to what came before.
  3. How it works: the core idea, with a diagram where one helps.
  4. How to use it: setup and a working example.
  5. Trade-offs and limits: when not to use it, maturity, cost and licensing.
  6. Where it fits: links to the related notes in this knowledge base.
  7. Questions to test yourself and Sources.

2. Notes

Newest first. Each row links to the note and gives the date it was added.

# Date Note In one line
006 2026-10-10 Python 3.15 Lazy imports, frozendict, UTF-8 by default and a faster JIT, plus an upgrade checklist

003 2026-10-06 GitHub Copilot code review via API Request AI reviews from automation, and four Copilot models retired
